name: @kitora/upload
description: Kitora's files and media kit: a dropzone with validation, an upload queue on a pluggable (and chunked, resumable) adapter, an image cropper, avatar upload, a media library, and image, PDF, video and audio viewers.

exports.name: formatBytes
exports.description: `1536` → `"1.5 KB"`. Whole bytes stay whole; larger units keep one decimal under 10.

exports.name: formatDuration
exports.description: Seconds → `m:ss`, or `h:mm:ss` past an hour. Non-finite input (a live stream) → `--:--`.

exports.name: formatRate
exports.description: Bytes per second → `"1.2 MB/s"`.

exports.name: extensionOf
exports.description: The lower-cased extension without the dot (`"Report.PDF"` → `"pdf"`), or `""`.

exports.name: UploadFormatters
exports.description:
The display seam: every styled surface formats sizes, durations and rates
through one of these, so a host can switch to SI units, a locale's number
format or its own wording with one `UploadFormatProvider` instead of
forking components. {@link DEFAULT_FORMATTERS} is the kit's own.

exports.name: DEFAULT_FORMATTERS
exports.description: The kit's formatters: binary units, `m:ss`, `"<size>/s"`.

exports.name: parseAccept
exports.description: Parses the accept grammar into lower-cased tokens.

exports.name: acceptMatches
exports.description:
True when `file` matches the accept string. Tokens are `.ext`, `type/*` or an
exact MIME type. A file with an empty `type` (the browser could not tell)
can still match by extension.

exports.name: describeAccept
exports.description: A short human label for the accept string (`"images, .pdf"`), for hints and errors.

exports.name: validateFile
exports.description: Every per-file rule `file` breaks (the count rule is batch-level, see {@link validateBatch}).

exports.name: validateBatch
exports.description:
Splits an incoming batch into accepted and rejected files. `held` is how many
files are already in the queue, so `maxFiles` counts the total; once full,
every further valid file is refused with `too-many-files` (files keep their
order, so the first ones dropped win the slots).
exports.signature: <F extends FileLike>(files: readonly F[], rules: UploadRules, held?: number) => { readonly accepted: readonly F[]; readonly rejected: readonly Rejection<F>[]; }

exports.name: fileKind
exports.description: Classifies a file by MIME type, falling back to its extension.

exports.name: FileLike
exports.description: The minimal file shape validation reads; a DOM `File` satisfies it.

exports.name: UploadRules
exports.description: What the dropzone accepts. Every field is optional; an empty object accepts anything.

exports.name: REJECT_CODES
exports.description: Why a file was refused. A closed set, so a host can translate or branch on it.

exports.name: RejectCode
exports.description: One of {@link REJECT_CODES}.

exports.name: Rejection
exports.description: A refused file with every reason it failed.

exports.name: FILE_KINDS
exports.description: The broad kind of a file, for icons, previews and library filters.

exports.name: FileKind
exports.description: One of {@link FILE_KINDS}.

exports.name: abortError
exports.description: The error every shipped adapter rejects with on abort; test for it with {@link isAbortError}.

exports.name: isAbortError
exports.description: True for a cancellation (ours or the platform's `fetch`/XHR AbortError), so a queue can tell cancel from failure.

exports.name: delay
exports.description: Resolves after `ms`, or rejects with {@link abortError} as soon as `signal` aborts.

exports.name: createChunkedAdapter
exports.description:
Sends a file chunk by chunk. After every acknowledged chunk it records the
offset, so a later `upload` of the same file (a retry after an error, or
after a cancel) skips straight to the first unacknowledged byte.
exports.signature: <F extends Blob = File>(options: ChunkedAdapterOptions<F>) => UploadAdapter<F> & { readonly store: ResumeStore; }

exports.name: createFakeAdapter
exports.description: A whole-file adapter with simulated progress, for demos and tests.

exports.name: createFakeTransport
exports.description: A chunk transport with simulated network time, for showing resume.

exports.name: UploadProgress
exports.description: Bytes sent so far out of the total.

exports.name: UploadResult
exports.description: What a finished upload hands back; every field is optional because backends differ.

exports.name: UploadContext
exports.description: Per-call context: cancellation and progress reporting.

exports.name: UploadAdapter
exports.description: The one seam between the kit and a storage backend.

exports.name: ChunkTransport
exports.description: A backend that takes a file in pieces (tus, S3 multipart, GCS resumable, your own API).

exports.name: ResumePoint
exports.description: How far a file got: its session and the bytes the backend acknowledged.

exports.name: ResumeStore
exports.description: Where resume points live; a `Map` works, so does a wrapper over IndexedDB or localStorage.
